newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium futures surge on Russian factor.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium futures surge on Russian factor.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended sharply higher on Friday, as a delay in starting Russia-Japan talks continued to impact the market, traders said. Other metals ended mixed to easier.

All palladium futures hit record highs. The April, December and October contracts skyrocketed by their 22 yen per gram daily limit during the day. Benchmark December futures ended up 19 yen at 514 yen.
Traders said the outlook for palladium remained bullish until the timing of the resumption of Russian exports become clear.
In buoyant trade, animated short-covering by individual investors and trade house buying buoyed futures before profit-taking put a lid on further gains later in the day, the traders said.

Spot palladium was quoted at a nearly six-month high of $130.00/131.00 per ounce, against Thursday's London fixing of 129.00. One trader said it was highly likely that spot palladium would reach $135.00 in the very near future.
In contrast with palladium's sparkle, trading in other precious metals was lacklustre as most players were tending to retreat to the sidelines, the traders said.
Gold futures ranged from one yen to 10 yen per gram lower, depressed by weaker bullion prices. Most-active benchmark December was off three yen at 1,354 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $341.90/342.40 per ounce, against $342.80/343.30 in New York on Thursday.
Silver futures were mixed, coming off early lows as the dollar's rises gained momentum in the afternoon. Benchmark December silver was up 0.1 yen per 10 grams at 194.0 yen.
Benchmark December platinum was down one yen at 1,376 yen.
